This is correct — the recipe doesn't prescribe depth — but the meta-note signals a potential future ADR (recipe scale-appropriateness). Not a deviation; just worth recording for future.

soft_observations.what: Synthesis stage produced a lightweight fan-in (not the full 6-agent synth-* chain) appropriate to the feature's research surface (1 external + 1 codebase analysis). Self-noted in synthesis.md as 'no scope deviation' because the recipe doesn't prescribe depth.
soft_observations.implication: If a future feature run hits the same scale-mismatch (recipe specifies synth-* chain; reality has small research surface), an ADR codifying 'scale-appropriate synthesis' would be worth authoring. Out of scope for this feature.

soft_observations.topic: auditing-shared SKILL.md will be loaded by audit dispatch context
soft_observations.what: ADR-0031 notes that SKILL.md will be loaded if Claude scans the skill registry; correctly notes the SKILL.md must be small + clearly marked as utility module.
soft_observations.implication: Per-layer Design's SKILL.md authoring task should keep the file tightly scoped (≤30 lines) and use unambiguous 'not directly invocable' language to prevent confusion in agent contexts.
soft_observations.action: Plan stage / per-layer Design author the SKILL.md with this constraint in mind.

soft_observations.topic: D-3 substance-keyword list extensibility process is in spec, not ADR
soft_observations.what: Q-CC-6 resolution puts the extension procedure in the mechanism-α spec rather than requiring an ADR per extension. This is correct (extensions are minor) but the spec must clearly establish the extension protocol (who reviews, what evidence is needed).
soft_observations.implication: FR-7-a spec authoring must include an explicit 'Extending the keyword list' subsection. Per-layer Design should pre-stage this; Plan stage tasks it.
soft_observations.action: FR-7-a spec authoring task includes Extension Procedure subsection.
